beats.t: The stairs ended in a round chamber beneath the temple. Though it had no ceiling, rain fell. Before reaching the floor, the water caught on red threads and ran along them.
A black tiger sat in the center. A chain led from the golden ring around its neck into a crack in the floor. Beneath that crack, a scaled tail stirred slowly.
Found you.
Wow. Really here. Much bigger than I expected, though.
We have four on our side. We can win on numbers.
Have we ever won on numbers?
Today's our first match.
You found me. Holding that thread so tightly, for someone who came to confront me.
I did come to confront you. I have a list.
Yeoni opened their notebook. The tiger's golden eyes followed it. For a brief instant, those eyes narrowed like a hungry beast's.
One: the drummer child's applause. Two: the voices of the Island of Expression. Three: counting my socks from next door.
That last one is a little unfair.
I'm the one treated unfairly! You talked at the wall about my socks not matching!
Yeoni. Is that important right now?
All of it is. I'm going through it one thing at a time.
The tiger didn't laugh. Instead, the chain jerked once. Its neck bent downward. Its breathing was rough.
Four. You wrote down that I saved you too, I hope. The day hands came out of your phone.
...I did. I'm asking about that too.
You're taking issue with being saved?
Why you saved me. Until I hear that, I can't ask about the rest.
Yundal whispered behind Yeoni, lifting his gloved hand slightly to indicate the chain on the floor.
My lady. That chain is attached directly to the tail. Break it by force, and the tail wakes.
The tail eats the past. If it wakes, it'll eat her memories first.
Then what? Just leave it and talk?
Talk first. That beast is under orders right now. Look at its eyes.
A black dot floated inside the tiger's golden eyes, like a tiny eclipse. Whenever it grew, the tiger's claws scraped the floor.
There's no time. I'm being told to empty you, Yeoni. Inside my head. Constantly.
Empty me? Empty what?
Starting with what you hold on to until the end.
A black forepaw flashed out. The notebook vanished from Yeoni's hands. The tiger pinned it beneath its paw.
Hey! Give that back!
Moka, wait. Those eyes are fighting right now. Not out here. Inside.
The tiger didn't tear the notebook. It didn't extend its claws. It simply turned the pages with its forepaw. One, then another.
Every page was crowded with Yeoni's awkward handwriting. Other people's names, other people's circumstances. Skewer counts, birthdays, before the rooster crowed, left arm.
The tiger's paw stopped on one page. A line pressed heavily into the paper twice: Seo Hanbi. Dragged away. Must find her.
When did you write this?
At the palace of stars. As soon as I heard you being dragged away.
The tiger turned another page. There it was again: Drummer child's name. Inside tiger's cloak. And a little question mark.
You wrote this down too. What I hid.
I thought you were keeping it safe, not hiding it. That's why I added the question mark. Because I don't know yet.
The tiger's breath stopped. The black dot in its eye wavered. It began to grow, then halted.
I said names were debts. That speaking one makes you indebted. So why did you write my name so large?
To owe you.
What?
People in debt have to meet again. To repay or collect. So I put myself in your debt on purpose. Yours, Seo Hanbi.
The tiger couldn't answer. It had filled thousands of ledger pages. Yet it had never seen arithmetic like this.
Yeoni's logic is scarier than a loan shark's.
From today on, I'm never borrowing money from my lady.
Only Neo didn't smile. He watched the tiger for a long time. Less like someone guarding against an enemy than someone recognizing another person caught in the same day's rain.
Remember the last scene of that spring. Not what you saw. What was actually there.
What do you know? That spring, you arrived too late.
Yes. I was late. That's why I came early this time.
(Arrived late? Neo? That spring?)
Let me ask one thing. Answer it, and I'll give this back.
Ask.
On a rainy day, if there's only one umbrella, what do you do?
Yeoni didn't think. It wasn't a question that needed thought.
Half each. Obviously.
The tiger's forepaw trembled. The notebook slipped to the floor. Something fell from its golden eye. Rainwater or something else—it was impossible to tell.
Half each. Why are you the one saying that?
The red thread around Yeoni's wrist suddenly blazed. Its other end was wound around the tiger's right forepaw, above the mark left by a ring.
A scene appeared in the light. A bus stop. One umbrella. A packet of gummies. Two children's wet sneakers. Yeoni saw it too.
This is what I saw in the twelfth house. The bus stop.
You can see it too, Yeoni?
(This isn't my memory. Then why do I know how the umbrella handle feels? Why do I know the gummies are grape-flavored?)
A thread from another life. You two met in that life.
What did they do in that life? Fight?
No one could answer. The scene stopped halfway through instead of reaching its end: the girl with the umbrella turning away. Everything after that had been blacked out.
Then Yeoni looked at the thread leading from their wrist to Neo. It was thinner than before. Only one fiber remained.
Neo. The thread.
I'm fine. Look over there first.
Neo's right arm was empty all the way to his shoulder. He turned to hide it, but the red rain passed straight through.
If not now, when? You keep saying later!
Yeoni. That beast is disobeying its orders for the first time. Look at that. My paw isn't running away.
...It is. Little by little. Right in front of me.
The sky opened. Above the roofless chamber rose an enormous head with no body, cleanly severed below the neck.
The head is hungry. The tail holds many memories. Because of you, both have starved, vessel.
The head opened its mouth. One moon was sucked into it: the Moon of Bharani, the Ram's second house.
Ah... My stomach.
Yeoni dropped to their knees. Their stomach felt hollow, as though the place that had held something had collapsed all at once.
Yeoni! Stay with us!
Tiger. Now. Empty that child. Down to the very last thing.
No.
One short word. The room fell silent. Even the rain seemed to stop.
Say that again.
I said no. The emptier that child becomes, the fuller you grow. I didn't put on this leash to serve your meals.
Then why did you wear it? Do you remember?
To stop her. Before she became a monster.
Yes. Before that child became a monster. And what is that child now?
The tiger looked at Yeoni. A twenty-three-year-old woman sitting on the floor, clutching her stomach. A person with thread around her wrist, still holding it in the hand that had lost the notebook.
...She doesn't look like a monster. Not at all.
Your eyes have clouded. Because of the rain.
No. They've finally cleared.
The floor shook. The tail beneath the crack woke. The chain tugged wildly, dragging the tiger toward the gap.
Tail. Eat that child's bygone spring. Without memories, there is no reason to rebel.
Now. Mr. Cat, don't stop me.
Yundal removed his glove and aimed the hole in his palm at the chain. Its black energy streamed into the hole. The chain slackened a little.
I'll help! Fire ought to startle a tail!
Moka pulled matches from his apron pocket. They wouldn't light in the rain. Three tries, four. Only on the fifth did a tiny flame appear.
He held the flame to a chain link. The metal glowed red. The tail flinched and briefly loosened its grip.
See? A chef can light a fire even in the rain.
Moka, that was genuinely impressive. Shall I read our compatibility?
You're bringing that up now?!
Yeoni, grab the thread. The one leading to that beast.
Yeoni couldn't stand. Still, they reached out and wound the red thread around both hands. It cut into their palms.
I'm not letting go. I still have a mountain of questions.
Let go. The tail will eat you too.
Then it can eat us together. Half each, remember? You said it.
The tiger was sucked into the crack. At the last moment, its golden eyes met Yeoni's. The black dots were gone.
The thread didn't snap. It stretched taut into the gap. Something flowed back up along it: the sound of old rain. The scent of a long-ago spring.
(This isn't my memory. It's hers. But I can hear my name.)
Yeoni. That thread leads to the first spring.
Then we follow it. All of us. I'll ask every question there, one by one.
